thesis: One dense Spanish typographic page whose only machinery is the machinery that carries evidence — a type system that refuses to compile an unsourced claim, a BASE_URL asset helper that makes two real figures resolve on GitHub Pages, and a footnote grammar borrowed from print — betting that a reader who can click any sentence to its source in one hop trusts the page more than a reader who can navigate it.

evidenceModel: Evidence is a required field on the type, so an unsourced claim does not compile. `src/content.ts` is rewritten as `Project = { name, status, statusSource, lede, ledeSource, claims: Claim[], figure? }`, with `Claim = { text: string; evidence: Evidence }` and `Evidence` a discriminated union `repo | live | doc | figure`, each carrying an https URL (or a figure id resolved through a frozen `FIGURES` map). `evidence` is NOT optional anywhere, so `tsc --noEmit` — already an M4 gate command — becomes the first M1 instrument: adding a sentence about a project without attaching a source is a type error, not a review oversight. `src/content.test.ts` closes the rest and PRODUCES the number instead of asserting it in prose: exactly 5 projects; every `status` equal to a frozen literal transcribed from that project's README; every evidence URL parsing under `new URL()` with protocol `https:`; every figure id present in `FIGURES`; and a computed `claims-with-evidence / claims` fraction. On the page, `EvidenceLink` renders each claim's source as a trailing footnote-style anchor in mono — `[README §Estado]`, `[MEASUREMENTS.md · 2026-07-31]`, `[sw/hwcheck.s]`, `[syn/VENDOR_VS_ESTIMATE.md]` — pointing at that exact file in that project's own repo. The reader goes claim → proof in one click without leaving the sentence, which is the print-footnote grammar the angle is built on rather than a badge or a card. The two figures are zero-click evidence, each wrapped in an `<a>` to the full-resolution PNG so the small in-column rendering is one click from legible. The `<details>` block per project holds the reproduction instructions (`python syn/build_vendor.py`, `testbench.ps1`, `npm run coverage`) as `Claim[]` too, so the same type gate covers them. Three things this model deliberately cannot do, stated rather than papered over: it cannot verify that the URLs resolve over the network (that is the quality veto's check and it is in contentGaps); it cannot verify GitHub's generated heading-anchor slugs offline; and it does not extend to the header identity line or the tools list, because M1's enumeration unit is an assertion about a project — the tools list is nonetheless written so every row names the project that evidences it, which closes that gap by construction rather than by argument.

contentGaps: Link resolution cannot be verified from here. I have no network, so I cannot confirm that github.com/Swately/Phyriager, /PhyriadFG, /Phynned, /PHarvard and /climx are public and resolve — the objective's quality veto ('every link resolves') therefore has an unverified precondition that the operator must check once. PHarvard is the sharpest case: its README says the repo was renamed from Hardvard-Processor on 2026-08-01 and that existing links survive on GitHub's redirect, which is a redirect this page would be relying on.

GitHub heading-anchor slugs for the deep source links. The evidence model points claims at specific README sections (e.g. climx §'Why it's built the way it is', Phyriager §Status, PhyriadFG §'Honest scope', PHarvard §State). GitHub generates those fragment slugs and I cannot verify them offline; each needs one check, and any that fails degrades that claim from a section link to a whole-file link.

The page's own measured numbers do not exist yet. The colophon prints the bundle gzip size, the CSS size, the test count and the single-view transferred bytes — none of which exist until M-D and M-E run. Until then the colophon must not be written with placeholder figures, per the discipline it is borrowing from MEASUREMENTS.md ('No entry, no claim').

Three of five projects have no image, and no honest one exists on disk. There is no screenshot of climx live, of Phynned's UI, or of PHarvard's board/display — the objective confirms this and I found nothing to contradict it. So the page is visually uneven by construction: PhyriadFG and Phyriager carry figures and the other three carry only prose and numbers. weakestPoint: My M6 has no margin under a hostile-but-fair recount, and the cause is the angle itself. Of the seven pool resources I count, three (primitives, tokens.css, toolchain) were already in the portfolio before this design existed, so a judge who reads M6 as measuring what a candidate *does* rather than what the finished page *contains* immediately strikes them and I am at four — exactly the target, zero headroom. Of those four, two are individually contestable and I would contest them myself: public/404.html is climx's deep-link shim with its entire reason for existing removed, since there is no router to restore a path into, and MEASUREMENTS.md is content rather than code, admissible only because the objective's own candidate pool lists it. Strike both and I am at two, which does not merely lose on M6 — it trips K2 and disqualifies the design outright. So the honest summary is that D3's declared handicap is not a headwind, it is a cliff edge: forgoing the router forgoes the pool's one unambiguous, uncontestable, capability-granting resource, and everything I reach for instead is smaller and more arguable. I could have closed this in one move by adding a /lab route to collect the router, the router test suite, NotFound and PrimitivesLab — four resources, all uncontestable, still inside E8's four-route bound. I did not, because that move stops being an editorial single page and starts being D2 wearing D3's typography, and because the objective states plainly that M6 is a floor rather than a maximand and that P2 cannot be farmed. That is the right call for the search — the judges need this angle pushed to its real conclusion — but it means my design is the one candidate whose survival depends on how a judge reads a metric definition rather than on what the page does for its reader. A distant second weakness, worth naming because it is structural to the angle rather than to the count: one page is one view, so all 257 KB of my two figures land in a single M3(b) budget, and the design has no room to grow visually without spending the headroom that the operator's three missing screenshots would need.
